reviewedAgainst: RC18 original + RC30 eight-record append-only overlay
policy: Preserve dated IUCN and DENR status independently. One or more facts in a section does not prove completeness. Original morphology is limited to sampled type series. National category is the dated 2019 administrative listing. Avoid converting island/historic vouchers into live occupancy. Photographs are not embedded without approved license and species-identification audit.

records.label: Northern rufous hornbill forest context
records.text: Northern Rufous Hornbills inhabit extensive primary rainforest and mature secondary forest, with records extending from lowlands to approximately 2,100 m.
records.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group (n.d.), Northern Rufous Hornbill
records.sourceLocation: Habits section
records.studyScope: Broad species synthesis; elevation is reported occurrence, not a local survey range or modeled habitat preference.

records.label: Northern species island range
records.text: The Northern Rufous Hornbill is reported on Luzon and Marinduque. Records of the Southern Rufous Hornbill on Mindanao and Eastern Visayas belong to a separate species account.
records.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group (n.d.), Northern Rufous Hornbill
records.sourceLocation: Distribution section; see separate Southern Rufous Hornbill species account
records.studyScope: Uses the split northern versus southern species concepts. Do not merge the historical broad Buceros hydrocorax complex with present northern range.

records.label: Fruit feeding and canopy foraging
records.text: The diet is mainly fruits and seeds, including figs, with insects and centipedes recorded as animal food; foraging usually takes place in large forest-tree canopies.
records.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group (n.d.), Northern Rufous Hornbill
records.sourceLocation: Habits section, food and foraging
records.studyScope: Secondary specialist synopsis, not quantified year-round food composition for any particular forest.

records.label: IUCN global category reported for 2020
records.text: The Hornbill Specialist Group reports a 2020 IUCN global assessment of Vulnerable (VU) for the Northern Rufous Hornbill under criterion A2cd+3cd+4cd.
records.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group (n.d.), Northern Rufous Hornbill, citing IUCN 2020
records.sourceLocation: Red List Status, 2020 IUCN assessment as transcribed by specialist group
records.studyScope: The specialist page relays the dated IUCN status; check IUCN for future reassessments. Not the DENR national category or a population estimate.

records.label: DENR 2019 national threatened-fauna listing
records.text: DENR Administrative Order 2019-09 lists Buceros hydrocorax as Endangered (EN) in the Philippine national threatened-fauna list.
records.source: Department of Environment and Natural Resources (2019), DAO 2019-09
records.sourceLocation: Section 3, Category B Endangered, Birds, Bucerotidae
records.studyScope: Applies to the 2019 Philippine national listing and its taxon concept. Do not interpret national EN as IUCN VU, or as a statement that a 2026 legal review has taken place.

records.label: Writhed hornbill lowland forest ecology
records.text: Writhed Hornbills inhabit primary lowland rainforest, principally below 500 m, with records extending to about 1,100 m.
records.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group (n.d.), Writhed Hornbill
records.sourceLocation: Habits section, habitat and elevation
records.studyScope: Reported broad ecological occurrence, not a proven elevation limit for all Mindanao forests.

records.label: Writhed hornbill island records
records.text: The species is recorded from Mindanao and nearby Dinagat, Siargao and Camiguin islands.
records.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group (n.d.), Writhed Hornbill
records.sourceLocation: Distribution section
records.studyScope: Island-level literature summary, not a new sighting or station occupancy record.

records.label: Fruit seeking, canopy feeding and insect hawking
records.text: Writhed Hornbills feed mainly on fruit in the upper tree canopy; the specialist account records occasional insects captured in flight and movement between fruiting and roosting trees.
records.source: IUCN SSC Hornbill Specialist Group (n.d.), Writhed Hornbill
records.sourceLocation: Habits and food sections
records.studyScope: Unquantified specialist synthesis, not a measured diet proportion across every season.

records.label: IUCN dated Near Threatened assessment
records.text: The 9 September 2020 global IUCN assessment classified the Writhed Hornbill as Near Threatened (NT), criterion C1; the published assessment described risks from habitat loss and exploitation.
records.source: BirdLife International (2020), IUCN Writhed Hornbill assessment
records.sourceLocation: Assessment Information, date assessed 9 September 2020, global category and justification
records.studyScope: Dated 2020 IUCN global category. Not a DENR national assessment or a 2026 current population estimate.

records.label: Scarlet-collared flowerpecker forest use
records.text: Published assessment habitat notes describe closed-canopy forest chiefly below 1,000 m, with some records from logged or secondary forest, edges and fruiting trees in patches.
records.source: BirdLife International (2016), IUCN Scarlet-collared Flowerpecker
records.sourceLocation: Habitat and Ecology section of 1 October 2016 assessment
records.studyScope: Historic assessment habitat description, not current occupancy or a verified present-day density.

records.label: Mindoro and Visayan island records
records.text: The 2016 assessment describes historical records on Mindoro and later records on Panay and Negros.
records.source: BirdLife International (2016), IUCN Scarlet-collared Flowerpecker
records.sourceLocation: Geographic Range, Range Description, 2016 assessment
records.studyScope: Island records from an older assessment; no inference that the species occupies all forests on those islands.

records.label: Fruiting and flowering-tree visits
records.text: The assessment describes visits to fruiting and flowering trees in forest patches and scrub; vocal notes include thin, high-pitched song and a hard tup-tup call.
records.source: BirdLife International (2016), IUCN Scarlet-collared Flowerpecker
records.sourceLocation: Identification Information and Habitat and Ecology sections
records.studyScope: Qualitative observations and described vocalizations, not a recorded site-specific call classifier or a complete food list.

records.label: IUCN status changed in 2024
records.text: The IUCN Red List 2024-2 status-change table records a change for Scarlet-collared Flowerpecker from Vulnerable (2023) to Near Threatened (2024).
records.source: International Union for Conservation of Nature (2024), Red List Table 7
records.sourceLocation: IUCN Red List 2024-2, Table 7, Dicaeum retrocinctum row
records.studyScope: A published 2024 global status change, not a claim that the old 2016 assessment is current or that the Philippine national category changed.

records.label: Montane and occasionally disturbed forest habitat
records.text: The 2024 IUCN account describes primary montane forest and occasional secondary or disturbed habitats; records mostly occur above 1,000 m on Mindanao.
records.source: BirdLife International (2024), IUCN Blue-capped Kingfisher assessment
records.sourceLocation: Habitat and Ecology; assessed 20 June 2024
records.studyScope: Reported sightings span a wider altitudinal range; 'usually above 1,000 m' is not a hard detection threshold.

records.label: Mindanao endemic range
records.text: The 2024 IUCN range account places the Blue-capped Kingfisher on Mindanao where suitable forest persists, including more localities than older records suggested.
records.source: BirdLife International (2024), IUCN Blue-capped Kingfisher assessment
records.sourceLocation: Geographic Range and Range Description, 2024 assessment
records.studyScope: Source documents island-level geographic extent, not a confirmed new occurrence at any user GPS station.

records.label: Predawn vocal behavior
records.text: Blue-capped Kingfishers are unobtrusive forest birds that commonly vocalize just before dawn; the assessment notes they can be overlooked in routine daylight observation.
records.source: BirdLife International (2024), IUCN Blue-capped Kingfisher assessment
records.sourceLocation: Identification Information and Habitat and Ecology
records.studyScope: Qualitative field synopsis, not a standardized detection probability or a playback protocol.

records.label: IUCN 2024 Least Concern category
records.text: A global IUCN reassessment dated 20 June 2024 lists the Blue-capped Kingfisher as Least Concern (LC), replacing the earlier Vulnerable classification. The same assessment describes a suspected decline.
records.source: BirdLife International (2024), IUCN Blue-capped Kingfisher assessment
records.sourceLocation: Global Assessment, date assessed 20 June 2024, status LC, previous 2016 VU
records.studyScope: Global IUCN LC is not proof of population security or the same as Philippine DENR status.

records.label: Agusan Marsh specimen context
records.text: An Agusan Marsh inventory documented Kaloula picta among non-peat and non-freshwater-swamp survey records, rather than from the study's peat-swamp sampling column.
records.source: Sanguila et al. (2026), ZooKeys 1272:203–251
records.sourceLocation: Table 1, Kaloula picta row: OS (other surveys); material examined at Bunawan
records.studyScope: One study's other-survey category, not proof that the species avoids peat or freshwater swamps or a quantified preference.

records.label: Published Bunawan voucher records
records.text: The 2026 Agusan Marsh inventory examined Kaloula picta vouchers KU 314056–57 from Barangay San Marcos, Bunawan, Agusan del Sur.
records.source: Sanguila et al. (2026), ZooKeys 1272:203–251
records.sourceLocation: Kaloula picta species account, Material examined
records.studyScope: Specific verified vouchers from eastern Mindanao, not a complete distribution range or an inference of present local occupancy.

records.label: Agusan Marsh identification characters
records.text: Specimens assigned to Kaloula picta in the 2026 Agusan Marsh account have an olive-brown dorsum with a large, variable dark medial marking, pale-brown to pinkish-tan underside, and webbed toes with little to no expansion of terminal discs.
records.source: Sanguila et al. (2026), ZooKeys 1272:203–251
records.sourceLocation: Kaloula picta Identification, Figure/specimen treatment
records.studyScope: Summary of a sampled series and earlier diagnostic literature; coloration is variable, so a single color mark is not a definitive field key.

records.label: Original diagnosis: high scale counts
records.text: The original diagnosis records 112–117 scales around the tail base, 152–157 around the midbody and 120–129 around the neck for the examined type series; juvenile dorsal spots form about twelve faint transverse rows.
records.source: Koch, Gaulke & Böhme (2010), Zootaxa 2446:1–54
records.sourceLocation: Varanus rasmusseni diagnosis, Figures 19–24 and comparative Table 3
records.studyScope: Type-series morphological measurements, not a photo-only identification criterion. Comparison requires specialist handling and measured scutellation.

records.label: Tawi-Tawi original type locality
records.text: The holotype and juvenile paratype of Varanus rasmusseni were collected at Tarawakan, north of Batu-Batu on Tawi-Tawi Island, in October and November 1961.
records.source: Koch, Gaulke & Böhme (2010), Zootaxa 2446:1–54
records.sourceLocation: Holotype and Paratype sections, 1961 type locality records
records.studyScope: Original specimen provenance, not evidence of present-day occupancy across the Sulu Archipelago.

records.label: Original specimen comparison with Luzon cloud rats
records.text: The 1981 original description distinguishes the single known Ilin Island Crateromys specimen from C. schadenbergi by smaller size and additional pelage, skull and jaw characters.
records.source: Musser & Gordon (1981), Journal of Mammalogy 62(3):513–525
records.sourceLocation: Abstract, diagnosis of the only Ilin specimen
records.studyScope: The original study documented one specimen, not a population-wide morphometric range. No photographed living comparison is implied.

records.label: Holotype provenance: Ilin Island
records.text: The 1981 species description is based on one specimen obtained from Ilin Island, southwest of Mindoro. The cited record alone cannot establish extant distribution.
records.source: Musser & Gordon (1981), Journal of Mammalogy 62(3):513–525
records.sourceLocation: Abstract, single type specimen and island provenance
records.studyScope: Purchased historical specimen with unknown original collection microhabitat; not a modern detection or site polygon.

records.label: DENR 2019 national Critically Endangered list
records.text: DENR Administrative Order 2019-09 lists Crateromys paulus among Philippine mammals in the Critically Endangered (CR) national category.
records.source: Department of Environment and Natural Resources (2019), DAO 2019-09
records.sourceLocation: Section 3, Category A Critically Endangered, Mammals, Muridae
records.studyScope: This is the Philippine 2019 national legal category, not an inferred IUCN global category or recent proof that living individuals exist.

records.label: Original nomenclature and species separation
records.text: Manuel and Gilliard published the replacement name Dicaeum kampalili in 1953 for the Mt. Kampalili flowerpecker. Clements subsequently separated the Mindanao species from the Luzon Yellow-crowned Flowerpecker D. anthonyi.
records.source: Manuel & Gilliard (1953), The Auk 70(1), Article 20
records.sourceLocation: The Auk 70(1), Article 20, replacement name; comparative interpretation in Clements v2023
records.studyScope: Nomenclature and taxonomic split, not a verified visual or vocal diagnostic character. A true key still requires original comparative descriptions or examined specimen images.
